title: Every unhandled rejection is reported to the user as a failed save
body:
## Summary
lib/GlobalErrorBridge.tsx routes EVERY unhandled promise rejection into the storage-trouble channel, so a non-storage failure is voiced and shown as "Not saved: the browser refused the operation. a background task was not written."

## Description
GlobalErrorBridge.tsx:27-29 calls `reportStorageTrouble("write", "app", "a background task", e.reason)` for any `unhandledrejection`. stepStore's `classify()` (app/_phases/_shared/stepStore.ts:222-226) maps anything that is not a quota/blocked/unavailable error to `failed`, and the bell renders `failed` as "the browser refused the operation" with the phase "a background task ... was not written" (components/ui/NotificationBell.tsx:51-59). The bridge's header argues the residual population is dominated by storage writes, but a void'd fetch rejecting (TypeError: Failed to fetch), an AbortError, or any thrown TypeError in fire-and-forget code lands in the same sentence - a wrong cause and a wrong remedy. Fixed looks like: a distinct trouble kind (or channel) for non-storage rejections carrying the reason's own message, so the bell says "a background task failed: <message>" and "Not saved" is reserved for storage-shaped errors (DOMException names, the IndexedDB sentences).

## Flow
- a component fires `void fetch(...)` and the network drops -> TypeError rejection, unhandled
- window `unhandledrejection` -> GlobalErrorBridge -> reportStorageTrouble("write","app","a background task", TypeError)
- classify() -> `failed` -> bell + announcer: "Not saved: the browser refused the operation. a background task was not written."
- the user checks storage/quota; nothing is wrong with storage

## Expected impact
A creator hearing a failure gets its real cause; screen-reader users especially, since this copy is voiced as blocking. Could break: the bell's five-kind vocabulary grows by one, and anything that switches exhaustively on StorageFailure must learn it.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - a non-storage failure is no longer reported as a failed save with a storage remedy
Before: 3 walked non-storage rejections (TypeError from fetch, AbortError, a thrown TypeError) all render as "Not saved: the browser refused the operation"; 1 walked QuotaExceededError renders correctly as quota
After: the 3 render as a background-task failure carrying their own message; the quota case unchanged
Method: simulation - three concrete rejection shapes walked through classify() and troubleAnnouncement(); a probe would need the new kind to exist first, and that lives outside this context
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
lib/GlobalErrorBridge.tsx:27-29 reportStorageTrouble("write", "app", "a background task", e.reason)
app/_phases/_shared/stepStore.ts:222-226 classify(): quota | blocked | unavailable | failed (everything else)
components/ui/NotificationBell.tsx:57-59 failed -> "the browser refused the operation"; `Not saved: ... ${phase} was not written.`
note: VETO 1: the honest fix adds a kind in app/_phases/_shared/stepStore.ts and copy in components/ui/NotificationBell.tsx, both outside app-infrastructure's paths

title: jobs.cancel rewrites a settled job as failed - settle guards, cancel does not
body:
## Summary
In lib/jobs.tsx `settle` refuses to touch a job that is not `running`, but `cancel` maps any job with that id to `failed` / "Stopped by you." regardless of status.

## Description
lib/jobs.tsx:550-556 `settle`: `if (!j || j.status !== "running") return;` - documented as "a late resolve after a cancel cannot resurrect it". lib/jobs.tsx:558-563 `cancel`: finds the job, clears the slot, and unconditionally rewrites status to `failed` with error "Stopped by you.". The mirror case - a late cancel after a settle - is unguarded: a `done` job with its result already landed is re-labelled failed in the tray. The one caller that can race it is app/_phases/research/guided/useEducationalResearch.ts:92-95 (`abortResearch` reads `run.jobId` then cancels). Fixed looks like the same guard settle has: `if (!j || j.status !== "running") return;`.

## Flow
- a research run settles `done` (bell: "Research returned")
- the user hits stop a beat later while `run.jobId` still names that job
- `cancel(jobId)` -> the done job becomes `failed`, error "Stopped by you." in the tray, results still on the notebook

## Expected impact
The tray stops contradicting the notebook for one race. Could break: nothing observable - a running job is still cancelled exactly as before.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - a settled job cannot be relabelled by a late cancel
Before: walked: cancel on a `done` job -> status `failed`, error "Stopped by you."; on a `running` job -> `failed` (correct)
After: the `done` job is untouched; the `running` case unchanged
Method: simulation - JobsProvider is React state, the Node lane has no renderer and the live lane refuses module-level claims; a source ratchet for a one-line guard would be coverage theatre
Result: better
Gate: none
note: VETO 3: no gate can witness JobsProvider state in either lane and none can be built at S

title: A forge commit that fails between its two index writes appends duplicate ledger rows on retry
body:
## Summary
`commitRun` in lib/foundry/store.ts appends one ledger row per decided candidate and only marks the run `committed` at the very end; a failure after the ledger write (the styles write, findings.md, run.json) leaves the run uncommitted, and the retry appends every row again.

## Description
lib/foundry/store.ts:261-276 pushes rows into ledger.json and writes it; :278-286 writes styles.json; :283 writes findings.md (plain writeFile, not atomic); :285-293 writes verdicts and run.json with `status: committed`. Nothing is keyed: a retry after a failure at :280+ re-runs the whole function, the guard at :230 still sees a non-committed run, and `ledger.rows.push` doubles every row for that run. The style evidence at :281 doubles the same way (its `keptScenes` Set hides that, but the rows are still there). Fixed looks like: ledger rows keyed by (run, scene, style, mechanism, seed) and evidence keyed by (run, scene, mechanism) upserted rather than pushed, so a commit is idempotent per run.

## Flow
- commit a run with N decided candidates -> ledger.json gains N rows
- styles.json write throws (disk full, EPERM from a watcher on Windows) -> 500, run.json still says `done`
- the operator commits again -> ledger.json holds 2N rows for the run, evidence lists doubled

## Expected impact
The versioned indices stay one row per decision; nothing changes on the happy path. Could break: nothing observable - an upsert on a fresh key is a push.

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - a retried commit cannot double the versioned indices
Before: walked: N decided, failure after the ledger write, retry -> 2N rows (each row identical on every key)
After: N rows; the second commit rewrites the same keys
Method: simulation - the store's index paths are `process.cwd()`-relative constants pointing at the TRACKED pipeline/foundry/{ledger,styles}.json, so a probe cannot exercise a commit without mutating versioned files; the instrument that decides it is an S-sized root override (a FOUNDRY_DIR env read, like NEXT_DIST_DIR in next.config.ts) that the round did not have budget to build
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
lib/foundry/store.ts:230  if (run.status === "committed") throw ...   // the only idempotency guard
lib/foundry/store.ts:262-268  for (const c of decided) ledger.rows.push({ run: id, scene, style, mechanism, seed, ... })
lib/foundry/store.ts:281  s.evidence.push({ run: id, scene: c.scene, mechanism: c.mechanism, ... })
lib/foundry/store.ts:285-293  run.status = "committed" written LAST
note: CARRY: approved, not built - needs the store-root override first (S), then a disk probe like foundry-store-disk

title: An extract run records the style ids it kept, not the ids the catalogue actually wrote
body:
## Summary
`commitExtractRun` suffixes a kept style's id when the catalogue already has it (`haze` -> `haze-2`) and returns the suffixed ids in `written`, but stamps the run with `committed.kept = ["haze"]` - so the run and the catalogue disagree about the name of the same style forever.

## Description
lib/foundry/extract/store.ts:341-343 computes `cid` with a collision suffix and :371 collects it into `written`; :375 writes `run.committed = { at, kept: kept.map((s) => s.id), rejected }` with the RUN-LOCAL ids. `ExtractCommitResult.written` (types.ts:284-290) exists precisely because the two can differ, but only the HTTP response carries it; the manifest on disk - what the Extract tab renders after a reload, and what the Dojo or a future 'open in catalogue' link would read - keeps the wrong name. Fixed looks like: `committed.written: string[]` (or `kept: {id, catalogueId}[]`) on the manifest, written beside `kept`.

## Flow
- commit a run whose kept style `haze` collides with an existing catalogue `haze`
- the response says written ["haze-2"]; run.json says committed.kept ["haze"]
- reload the tab: the run shows `haze` as committed; the catalogue has no `haze` from this run

## Expected impact
A run can name its own catalogue entries. Could break: nothing - an added optional field on `committed`.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - the manifest names the catalogue ids it produced
Before: walked collision case: committed.kept=["haze"], catalogue wrote "haze-2", manifest carries no "haze-2"
After: manifest carries written=["haze-2"]
Method: simulation - same instrument gap as the ledger finding: a commit probe must not write the tracked styles.json; the root override decides both
Result: better
Gate: none
note: CARRY: approved, not built - same store-root instrument as the ledger carry

title: The extract commit refuses a `failed` run that the forge commit would accept
body:
## Summary
`commitRun` (forge) accepts a run in `done` OR `failed`; `commitExtractRun` accepts `done` only and answers "The run is not finished." - a sentence that is false for a failed run and sends the operator to a retry that a permanently absent vendor cannot satisfy.

## Description
lib/foundry/store.ts:231 `if (!["done","failed"].includes(run.status)) throw ... "The forge is still running this run."`; lib/foundry/extract/store.ts:327 `if (run.status !== "done") throw new FoundryError("The run is not finished.", 409)`. A run the circuit breaker stopped after replicating three styles fully has real, human-judgeable material; exemplars already carry `settled` reasons so a kept style from a failed run is honest evidence. Fixed looks like: accept `failed` in the extract commit as the forge does, and say "still running" only for live stages. The Extract tab offers Commit only on `done` (app/foundry/ExtractView.tsx), so the server half alone changes nothing a user can reach.

## Flow
- the vendor goes away mid-run; the breaker trips at 3 -> status `failed`, 3 styles replicated
- the operator keeps two of them and tries to commit -> 409 "The run is not finished."
- retry cannot succeed (vendor gone); the material is stranded

## Expected impact
A failed run's finished styles can be committed, as the forge's can. Could break: nothing - verdicts already gate what is written.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - a breaker-failed run with finished styles can be committed
Before: walked: status `failed`, 3 replicated styles, 2 kept -> 409, 0 written
After: 2 written with their settle reasons on the exemplars
Method: simulation - the server half is a one-line guard change; the reachable half is the Extract tab's commit control, outside this context
Result: better
Gate: none
note: VETO 1: the user-reachable half is app/foundry/ExtractView.tsx's commit control, outside foundry-api's paths

title: No gate runs the repository's Python, and the instrument now exists
body:
## Summary
`.github/workflows/gates.yml` installs Node and nothing else, and both test lanes are
TypeScript, so no gate in this repository executes a line of Python -- including the
965 lines under `pipeline/foundry/` that run for hours on a GPU and then write a verdict.

## Description
Every gate is green and every gate is honest; the coverage hole is invisible because
nothing renders it. This round's five defects were found by hand and three of them by a
selftest written in the same session -- two of those falsified the README's two headline
promises (`Resumable by construction`, `a candidate that could not be graded is
unmeasured, never a pass`), which is the class a gate exists to hold.

`pipeline/foundry/selftest.py` now exists and is the missing instrument: 5 cases, under a
second, no GPU / ComfyUI / Ollama / network. Crucially it is STDLIB-ONLY -- verified by
re-running it with PIL, numpy, requests, httpx, cv2 and torch blocked at `__import__`, 5
cases green. Pillow and numpy are imported inside `crop_letterbox` and `publish`, and the
`../vlm-probe` modules it pulls in have no module-level third-party imports.

That matters for THIS repo's own doctrine. gates.yml grades jobs on input determinism, not
severity: a job needing `pip install` from a public index is nominally external and
unpinned, so it could only be advisory. A job that is `setup-python` + `python
pipeline/foundry/selftest.py` has the same input shape as `typecheck` -- this tree's
sources plus a pinned interpreter -- and may BLOCK.

Fixed means: a `python` job in gates.yml at blocking severity, with the determinism
paragraph written beside it in the file's own idiom.

## Flow
- a session edits `pipeline/foundry/*.py` -> `npm test` is green -> CI is green -> merged
- nothing has run the changed code; the next run of it is an evening of GPU
- with the job: the same edit runs 5 cases in under a second, red on a break

## Expected impact
Whoever next touches this directory. The three defects this round's selftest caught were
each a total loss of a multi-hour run. One sentence on what could break: the job pins a
Python version, so an interpreter bump becomes a gates.yml edit -- which is the point.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - the repository's second language moves from 0 gate coverage to a blocking gate.
Before: 0 of 965 Python lines executed by any gate; 5 defects in the swept context, 3 of them findable by a sub-second check nobody could run.
After: selftest.py runs 5 cases green in <1s with every third-party package blocked at import, so a CI job needs no dependency step and is input-deterministic under gates.yml's own grading.
Method: probe - the selftest was built and run in-session under a blocked-import shim; what is NOT done is the gates.yml job itself, which is why this is a card and not a commit.
Result: better
Gate: architecture - .github/workflows/gates.yml and the CI job graph are outside this context's declared file_paths (veto 1), and adding a language to the build is the owner's call even with the determinism analysis done.
evidence:
.github/workflows/gates.yml — jobs: install (npm ci), typecheck, lint, manifest, test; no python step
package.json — "test": playwright golden-path; "test:live": playwright live. Both TypeScript.
$ git ls-files | grep -c '\.py$'   ->  Python files tracked, executed by 0 gates

$ python -c "<shim blocking PIL, numpy, requests, httpx, cv2, torch at __import__>" \

title: A run that gave up mid-generation still reports `done`
body:
## Summary
When `stage_generate` cannot recycle ComfyUI after a failure it `break`s out of the
candidate loop, leaving the rest `pending`; `main()` then completes normally and writes
`status: "done"` to the manifest the page reads.

## Description
`forge.py:330` — `if not guard.recycle_comfy("after failure"): break`. The function
returns, `stage_grade` scores what exists, and `main()` sets `manifest["status"] = "done"`
unconditionally at `forge.py:405`. A run that abandoned 80 of 90 candidates is
indistinguishable, in the one field the API reads as a lifecycle state, from one that
finished.

It is not invisible: `lib/foundry/store.ts:144` counts `graded` and `:245` counts
`unmeasured + failed`, and the FAILED lines are in `manifest["log"]`. So the operator CAN
reconstruct it — from a count that does not add up, and a log they have to open. What is
missing is the state itself.

Fixed looks like an `incomplete` (or a non-breaking `stopped_early` field) set when any
candidate is still `pending`/`failed` after generation, and the page saying so.

## Flow
- ComfyUI dies and will not restart -> `break` at forge.py:330
- stage 2 grades the plates that exist; main() marks the manifest `done`
- /foundry shows a finished run; the missing 80 are visible only as a shortfall in a count

## Expected impact
The operator culling the run. Measured by whether a partial run is distinguishable from a
complete one without opening the log: today no, after yes. What could break: `RunStatus` is
a closed union with consumers in two other contexts, so a new member is a contract change
across all of them.

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - a run's lifecycle state stops lying about whether the run finished.
Before: 1 of 1 abandoned-generation runs reports `status: "done"`; the shortfall is derivable only from candidate counts and the log.
After: not measured — the fix cannot be applied from inside this context, so no After figure was taken.
Method: simulation - the `break` path and main()'s unconditional `status = "done"` were read against the three consumers `RunStatus` is enumerated for; not run, because reproducing it needs a ComfyUI that refuses to restart.
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: contract - `RunStatus` in lib/foundry/types.ts:126 is a closed union consumed by lib/foundry/store.ts and the /foundry page (contexts foundry-api and foundry-ui), so consumers cannot be updated in the same commit from here (veto 1 + contract letter (a)).
evidence:
pipeline/foundry/forge.py:330   if not guard.recycle_comfy("after failure"): break
pipeline/foundry/forge.py:405   manifest["status"] = "done"        # unconditional
lib/foundry/types.ts:126        export type RunStatus = "created" | "annotating" | "generating" | "grading" | "done" | "failed" | "committed"
lib/foundry/store.ts:144        graded: m.candidates.filter((c) => c.status === "graded").length
lib/foundry/store.ts:245        const unmeasured = run.candidates.filter((c) => c.status === "unmeasured" || c.status === "failed")
lib/foundry/store.ts:256        if (!["done", "failed"].includes(run.status)) throw new FoundryError("The forge is still running this run.", 409)

title: The Python half of the build declares no dependencies anywhere
body:
## Summary
There is no `requirements.txt`, `pyproject.toml`, `setup.py` or `environment.yml` anywhere
in the repository, so a fresh clone cannot learn what the Python pipeline needs.

## Description
`git ls-files` matching those four names returns nothing. `pipeline/foundry/` needs Pillow
and numpy (imported lazily inside `crop_letterbox` and `publish`), and the `../vlm-probe`
modules it imports need whatever they need — which no file states either. The onboarding
overlay (`.claude/onboarding/config.md`) ladders eleven capabilities and every command in
it is `npx tsx …`; rung 8, the local-GPU rung, names `pipeline/vlm-probe/guard.py --status`
without saying what makes it importable.

This is the machine-specific half of the same hole the card above names: the manifest's
`repo.languages` says `[typescript]`, and both the CI and the onboarding ladder were
written from that. The Python is real, it is 965 lines in this context alone, and it is
undeclared.

Fixed looks like a `pipeline/requirements.txt` with pinned versions, named from the
onboarding ladder's rung 8 and from `.ai/manifest.yaml`.

## Flow
- a second machine clones the repo and follows the onboarding ladder
- every `npx tsx` capability comes up; rung 8 says to run a .py file
- `python pipeline/vlm-probe/guard.py --status` -> ModuleNotFoundError, with nothing to consult

## Expected impact
Anyone setting up a second GPU box. Measured as packages a fresh clone must guess: 2+ today
(Pillow, numpy, plus vlm-probe's own), 0 after. What could break: a pinned set that is wrong
is worse than none, so the pins must come from a machine where the pipeline actually runs.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - a fresh clone can install the Python half instead of guessing it.
Before: 0 dependency declarations for a language with 965 lines in this context; 2 third-party packages reachable by grep from these four files alone, and an unknown number behind ../vlm-probe.
After: not taken - the honest pin set is the one from the GPU rig where the pipeline is actually exercised, and this machine is not it (the manifest names `machine: secondary`).
Method: probe - enumerated third-party imports across the context's four files and the five vlm-probe modules they import; could not climb to `gate` because writing pins this box cannot verify would be the defect, not the fix.
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: none - but see the After line: the missing instrument is a `pip freeze` on the rig, which is the operator's machine, not a decision anyone here can substitute for.

title: Seven source-ratchet probes still carry the unsound comment stripper
body:
## Summary
`stripComments` landed in `tests/golden-path/_helpers.ts` (442e51f) and only the three
probes touched this round use it. Seven others still carry the private two-`replace`
pair, which hides a contiguous region of any file whose prose contains a route glob.

## Description
The pair strips block comments FIRST by regex, then line comments — so a block-open
sequence inside a LINE comment really opens a block, and it runs to the next genuine
terminator. This repo's prose is full of route globs written exactly that way.

Measured over 268 files under `app/` and `lib/`: 14 lose a region. `lib/imaging/api.ts`
80% of its bytes, `lib/imaging/types.ts` 78%, `lib/localMode.ts` 74%,
`app/_projects/ProjectDialog.tsx` 36%. Code in a hidden region is invisible to any probe
using the pair, and invisible code reads as a clean codebase.

The honest half, and the reason this is a card rather than a commit: NO probe in the
suite is blinded today. `object-url-ownership` hides 0 callers; all 26 API routes still
show their gate to `imaging-auth`; `dialog-closes-on-success`'s two anchors are visible
under both strippers. Every one of those was checked. This is a live hazard with no
current casualty — which is the moment to fix it, not evidence that it does not matter.

Fixed means: the seven adopt `stripComments` and delete their private copy.

## Flow
- someone adds a route glob to a line comment in a file a ratchet walks
- the ratchet silently stops seeing the rest of that file
- it goes green, and nothing distinguishes that from the rule being followed

## Expected impact
Whoever next trusts one of those probes. Measured as probes exposed to the hazard: 7
today, 0 after. What could break: nothing behavioural — but adopting it may turn a
currently-green ratchet red by making it see code it had been missing, which is the
point and should be read as a finding, not a regression.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - every source ratchet sees the whole file it is judging.
Before: 7 of 10 source-ratchet probes use the unsound pair; 14 source files carry a region invisible to them, up to 80% of a file.
After: not taken - the seven files belong to other contexts (imaging, projects, music, notebook, chrome), and adopting the helper means re-running each one and reading whatever new code it can suddenly see.
Method: probe - the exposure was measured exactly (the 268-file sweep above) and the three probes in THIS context were converted and re-verified red-then-green; the remaining seven were not touched.
Result: better
Gate: architecture - the seven probes guard other contexts' rules (veto 1), and adopting the helper can legitimately turn one red, which is a conversation with that context's owner rather than a silent edit.

title: Creating an extraction shrinks the whole gallery with no sign of progress
body:
## Summary
`startRun` re-encodes every dropped file one at a time before it posts anything, behind a
single boolean `creating`, so a gallery of any size is a silent wait with no count and no
way to tell it apart from a stall.

## Description
`app/foundry/ExtractView.tsx` — `for (const f of files) uploads.push(await prepareUpload(f));`
then one `createExtractRun`. `prepareUpload` decodes each file through `createImageBitmap`,
draws it to a canvas and re-encodes it to a JPEG data URL, which is real per-image work,
and the loop is fully serialized. Until the last one finishes the UI shows only whatever
`busy` renders in `NewRun`.

Fixed looks like a count as it goes ("shrinking 7 of 24") and, if it measures out, the
decode work overlapped rather than serialized.

## Flow
- drop a folder of gallery images -> press start
- every image is decoded, redrawn and re-encoded in sequence, one at a time
- nothing on screen changes until the POST goes out

## Expected impact
Anyone starting an extraction from more than a handful of images. Measured as time to
first feedback: currently the whole shrink pass, after it a tick per image. One sentence
on what could break: parallel decode raises peak memory, so overlapping is a separate
decision from reporting progress and should not be bundled with it.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - the operator can tell a working upload from a stalled one.
Before: 1 boolean for the whole pass; 0 progress signals across N images. The per-image cost was NOT timed.
After: not taken.
Method: simulation - read the loop and prepareUpload's three steps against how the surface is used (a folder of gallery images). The rung above needs a browser: createImageBitmap and canvas do not exist in the Node probe lane, and the live lane's header refuses claims a probe could witness — but a probe cannot witness this one either, so the honest instrument is a live-lane case with a fixture folder, which is more apparatus than this round could build.
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: none - the missing instrument is a live-lane fixture that drives the drop with N files and times to first feedback. That sentence is the next round's finding.

title: The outbox is 8 lines from its cap and nothing in this repo drains it
body:
## Summary
`.personas/memory-outbox.jsonl` reached 192 of its 200-line cap with this round. The next
sweep round cannot record its coverage nodes, and the one after cannot record findings.

## Description
The ingest caps at 200 lines / 512 KB / 30 finding lines and DELETES the file when the
Personas app ingests it. Nothing in this repository can trigger that — it is a UI action,
and four probes for a `/dev-tools/*` route that does it came back 404 (recorded in this
skill's overlay on 2026-08-29).

Three rounds this session appended ~36 lines each: 82 -> 120 -> 156 -> 192. Findings are
comfortably under their own cap (13 of 30); it is the LINE budget that binds, and most of
those lines are the per-lens coverage nodes the ledger's own rotation depends on.

The failure mode is the one the overlay already records happening five times: a round
silently drops what will not fit while the sweep ledger records the context as swept, so
the next picker believes coverage it does not have.

Fixed means: the operator ingests the file in the app, which deletes it.

## Flow
- a fourth round runs and appends ~36 lines
- the ingest cap is passed; whatever the round emitted beyond it is not recorded
- `.claude/scan-history/scan-sweep.jsonl` still says the context was swept at 28 lenses

## Expected impact
The next sweep, and any consumer reading coverage. Measured as headroom: 8 lines now, ~36
needed per round. What could break: nothing — ingesting is a read-and-delete.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - the sweep's own record stops being silently lossy.
Before: 192 of 200 lines, 13 of 30 findings, 8 lines of headroom against a ~36-line round.
After: 0 of 200 after an ingest — the app deletes the file.
Method: gate - counted the file directly at the start and end of each of the three rounds this session (82, 120, 156, 192) and against the documented cap.
Result: better
Gate: none - but nothing in this repo can do it. It is a UI action in the Personas app, so it is the operator's, not the run's.

control the shared `doClear` is wired to, and reasoning about whether Clear can strand a
job meant reading a file the round was not allowed to edit.

It also matters for coverage honesty: the ledger will record `research-step` as swept at
28 lenses while 790 of its 4,388 lines were only ever read, never judged for fixes.

Fixed means: a delta scan, which re-emits the context with those paths.

## Flow
- a sweep picks research-step and reads context-map.json for its file list
- guided/ is absent, so every finding there is veto 1
- the snapshot records the context swept; nothing records the 18% that was off-limits

## Expected impact
Every future sweep, conform and architect run on this context — six skills read this map.
Measured as declared coverage: 24 of 28 files today, 28 of 28 after. What could break: a
scan is a real model run and can duplicate a context (CLAUDE.md documents the verification
step), so it is not free.
